newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank may ease finance firm rates.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank may ease finance firm rates.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand is moving to standardise call interest rates for promissory notes issued by the country's 91 finance firms in a bid to halt bidding up of rates by cash-strapped firms, local media reported Wednesday.
But a central bank official told Reuters, when asked about the reports, that the authorities had no details of such a reported plan.

Newspapers quoted Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, a central bank official charged with supervising financial institutions, as saying he would seek ways of standardising short-term call rates paid by finance firms. He said finance companies had been hurt by rising rates in recent months due to a sustained liquidity crunch.
Thirachai was not available for comment.

Market confidence in the stability of some medium and small finance firms has declined this year amid concern that they may face cash-flow problems arising from an extended bearish stock market and a troubled property sector.
Industry sources said some finance companies had raised short-term funds by issuing promissory notes yielding over 20 percent interest a year to help tide them over cashflow problems.
